title: Head-to-Head Comparison of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Documentation Tools on Clinician Usability
official: Randomized Trial Protocol: Head-to-Head Comparison of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Documentation Tools on Clinician Usability
summary: This study is a pragmatic, randomized trial evaluating two ambient-listening virtual scribes among ambulatory care clinicians at UCLA Health. The primary aim is to determine whether perceived usability differs between two ambient scribe tools. Additional aims compare efficiency, note quality, clinician-reported experience with order queuing and coding support, diagnosis capture and order activity, safety, workload, adoption, productivity, and patient-reported communication experience. Given the absence of prior head-to-head data on these functions, hypotheses are non-directional.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Clinicians must practice at an outpatient UCLA Health Clinic(s); must have used Nabla within the preceding 90 days; and complete a baseline survey.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Physicians in training and clinicians with fewer than one half-day clinic session per week.
